title: PanDDA hit identification from many soaked datasets
summary: Collect many crystallographic datasets (over 30 unbound ground-state), align them, average the ground-state density, compute Z-maps and event maps with a background correction factor, and cluster significant regions to flag bound ligands. Method paper for the Pan-Dataset Density Analysis.

steps.text: Gather more than 30 ground-state datasets plus the soaked test datasets.
Align structures and maps using flexible alignment so that perfect isomorphism is not needed.
Build the ground-state model by averaging the density maps of unbound crystals in real space.
Compute per-point Z-scores for each test dataset against the ground-state ensemble; look for outliers (Z of about 2.5-3 or higher).
Generate event maps by subtracting an optimised fraction of the ground-state map (background density correction).
Cluster significant Z-score regions (minimum volume roughly 10 A^3) to nominate hits objectively.
Model the ligand and validate with RSCC > 0.7, RSZD < 3, sensible B-factors and RMSD < 1 A.

materials: Processed diffraction datasets and refined ground-state model
notes: No wall-clock durations stated, so none recorded. XChemExplorer (Krojer et al. 2017, PMC5349439, CC BY) wraps this workflow; its page was also opened but is not the primary source.
